intelligence.essence: RLQ Mutation Integrity Law: every critical revocation safeguard must be independently falsifiable. Deliberately removing an effective safeguard must produce a reachable, reproducible counterexample, unless another independently established safeguard prevents the violation. A model-checker PASS without mutation coverage is not sufficient proof. A verification harness is qualified only when it proves the correct model within its declared scope, detects deliberately broken behavior, and produces evidence showing exactly how each detected failure became possible. The goal is not red results for their own sake — it is demonstrating that the checker can tell the difference between a system that preserves current authority and one that merely appears to do so. A surviving mutant is not automatically failure: BLOCKED_BY_REDUNDANT_GUARD (independently verified) is a useful result; SURVIVED_UNEXPLAINED is not.
intelligence.falsifier: A PASS on a mutant whose defective branch was never exercised (UNREACHABLE counted as success); the implementation and the correctness definition mutated together; a mutant surviving with no established redundant guard; counterexamples averaged into a score; a stronger environmental assumption making a counterexample disappear without the assumption audit explaining why; an unreproducible counterexample treated as verified.

human_view.meaning: Trust, but verify — then verify the verifier. Take each safety guard and deliberately break it, one at a time: remove the publication check, remove the action fence, allow version numbers to go backwards, let recovery blindly restore old verdicts. For each sabotage, the checker must produce the exact crime scene — the shortest possible history showing how stale proof snuck back in. If it can't, the checker is blind and its green lights mean nothing. But there's honesty here too: if a second, independent guard catches the sabotage, that's not failure — that's defense in depth, properly credited. And the verdicts are strict: killed, blocked-by-backup-guard, survived-unexplained, never-reached, or unknown. Only 'killed' is the real prize. Then combine the sabotages, because real incidents don't come one at a time.

intelligence.learning_lesson: This is the falsification pattern made universal: the fairness layers got deliberately broken schedulers (SN-0771), the linearization law gets deliberately broken safeguards. The five-verdict taxonomy is the permanent contribution — it replaces binary pass/fail with an honest account of WHAT happened to each mutant, and it outlaws the two classic cheats (unexercised mutants counted as passes; implementation and oracle mutated together). Every future verification harness in NayaNET inherits this shape: prove the model, break the model, prove you caught the break.

M1 first (smallest model, central boundary), then M2/M3/M4. Compound mutations after isolated pass. Runtime integration tests with the refinement-argument limitation stated.

naya_view.directive: Separate the immutable reference specification from the mutated system and the independent history checker — never mutate the correctness definition with the implementation. Require activation witnesses; distinguish KILLED from BLOCKED_BY_REDUNDANT_GUARD from SURVIVED_UNEXPLAINED. Minimize counterexamples in two stages. Record each as a first-class receipt a cold successor can regenerate. Test compounds after isolated passes. Prove runtime behavior against the actual transaction engine with the universal-safety limitation honestly stated.

simple_view.meaning: Break each safety guard on purpose. The checker must catch every break with the exact crime scene — or the checker itself is broken.
